target_customer: Urban singles in NYC and SF who pay for matchmaker-arranged group dates
problem: Online dating feels impersonal and time-consuming; Dating Ring used human matchmakers to set up group dates so members only had to show up.
business_model: Consumer service sold per date or package, with human matchmakers

founders.name: Lauren Kay
prior_employers: Tutorly (consultant and acting CEO for six months, per YC page)
education: Brown University, class of 2011, American Civilization (Brown Alumni Magazine)
previous_startups: SmartSitting (babysitter and nanny matching, founded while a Brown sophomore; still majority owner)
founders.background_notes: Young adult writer represented at WME per YC page.

founders.name: Kate Bambino
prior_employers: Zynga (left to work on the company, per Brown Alumni Magazine)
education: Brown University, class of 2011 (Brown Alumni Magazine, listed as Katie Bambino)
founders.background_notes: Brown Alumni Magazine in March 2015 says she has since moved on.

founders.name: Emma Tessler
founders.background_notes: No bio found; named as co-founder by the YC page and Brown Alumni Magazine.

exit.reason: Company farewell page says it shut its doors on August 31, 2018 after five years; no cause is given.

competitors.name: Grouper
competitors.what: Group dates set up between friends without matchmaking, a YC alum

technical_complexity.rationale: A scheduling and booking product with human matchmakers; the hard part was operations, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Human matchmaking and group dates were easy to copy and Grouper already ran group dates; no data or network effect was described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source says an incumbent copied it; the company outlasted its YC batch by four years before closing in 2018.

market_need_then: Online dating fatigue and demand for higher touch matchmaking in cities; investors of the time were wary of dating startups, which an Andrew Chen post on why dating startups do not get funded discusses (title only seen in search results).

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, human: the site describes the team as real people looking for matches for you.

branding.brand_signature: Human matchmakers who act like friends
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in TechCrunch, Business Insider, Fortune and a 2015 podcast; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Steady press for a small startup but the name is descriptive and the sources show no distinctive asset.

outcome_analysis: Dating Ring was a YC W14 company that ran matchmaker-arranged group dates in New York and San Francisco and lasted about five years before closing on August 31, 2018. The company gave no cause, but sources show only small early funding (totals between 20K and 355K) and a category investors avoided, so the factors recorded are an inference from thin funding rather than a stated reason.
notes: Funding totals conflict: CB Insights lists one 20K seed on 2014-01-26 with Y Combinator; a Fortune piece (seen only as a search snippet) puts the total at 355K and another report cited 455K raised in March and May 2014; amounts and dates of those rounds were not found, so rounds may be missing. The 20K round rests on one database. CB Insights also carries a story that the founders declined a 50K offer at Demo Day, seen only as a headline. Failure factors are an inference, not a stated cause. Competitor list has one source dated February 2014, which is after the batch start of January 2014 by a few weeks only; later coverage of Coffee Meets Bagel, Hinge and Three Day Rule was dated 2015 or later and excluded.
